beats.say: You scan a code, type a PIN, and money moves in seconds. But no cash moved at all.
That code is just a payment address, like name at bank. Your app reads it and prepares a request.
The request goes to a central hub run by NPCI. Think of it as a traffic controller for payments.
The hub asks your bank one question: should this go through? Nothing moves until your bank answers.
Your UPI PIN is scrambled and goes only to your bank. It checks the PIN, and checks you have enough money.
Your bank says yes. The hub then tells the shop's bank to expect the money.
Now two records change. Your account goes down, and the shop's account goes up.
The banks settle up between themselves later, in bulk. No cash ever travels from one hand to another.
A moment later, both phones show a green tick. The whole trip usually takes just a few seconds.
